headline: TRUMP CANCELS IRAN STRIKES, SIGNALS HORMUZ DEAL "THIS WEEKEND" — Oil Plunges 4% to $86, Commodity Markets Begin Repricing
snippet: President Trump suspended planned U.S. military strikes against Iran late June 11 and told reporters a deal — including full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz — could be signed as early as this weekend in Europe; Brent crude immediately fell more than 4% toward $86/barrel, its lowest since April, marking the single largest relief move since the conflict began. For precious and base metals investors, the stakes are asymmetric: a confirmed Hormuz reopening removes the energy-cost shock driving May's 4.2% CPI print and the 70% probability of a December rate hike — the two inputs most responsible for gold and silver's 27% and 8% corrections from January peaks — while removing the supply chain premium that has supported an already structurally tight copper market.

headline: "EVERY BEARISH CATALYST LANDED AT ONCE — GOLD AND SILVER WENT UP ANYWAY": GoldSilver.com Flags Rare Resilience Signal
snippet: GoldSilver.com's June 11 analysis documents an unusual intraday event: on the same day the ECB hiked 25 basis points (its first rate increase since 2023), U.S. PPI printed at +6.5% year-over-year, and Iran war rhetoric intensified — conditions that on any prior day would have crushed precious metals — both gold and silver finished the session higher than their opening prints, with gold recovering from an intraday low near $4,080 to close above $4,200. The analysis interprets the resilience as evidence that the gold market has already front-loaded the hawkish macro pricing and is now trading on the other side of maximum pessimism, a setup that has historically preceded explosive relief rallies when a single data point — such as a Hormuz deal or a dovish Warsh dot plot — shifts the prevailing narrative.

headline: ENERGY FUELS HITS FULL-YEAR URANIUM TARGET BY JUNE 30 — 1.6M lbs at White Mesa, Only U.S. Conventional Mill, Stock +4.5%
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU / TSX: EFR) announced June 11 that its White Mesa Mill is on track to produce approximately 1.6 million pounds of finished U3O8 by June 30, 2026 — achieving the midpoint of the company's full-year guidance range of 1.5 to 2.5 million pounds in exactly six months, at a historic low processing cost of $9–$12/lb, the strongest utilization record in the mill's history. Processing will pause after the current campaign to rebuild ore stockpiles before resuming in Q4 2026 — a scheduled operational cadence, not a disruption — and shares rose 4.5% on the announcement to a market cap of approximately C$5.3 billion, with investors pricing in both the uranium milestone and the company's simultaneously advancing heavy rare earth element separation project at the same White Mesa mill infrastructure.

headline: NORTHISLE RED DOG: 216m AT 0.67% CuEq UNCOVERS NEW HIGH-GRADE EASTERN TREND — 800m STRIKE OPEN, PFS ON TRACK Q4 2026
source_name: Investing News Network / NorthIsle Copper and Gold
snippet: NorthIsle Copper and Gold Inc. (TSXV: NCX) released June 10 assay results from 8,112 metres of drilling at the Red Dog deposit on its North Island Porphyry Copper-Gold Project in British Columbia, identifying a newly emerging high-grade eastern mineralization trend with standout intercepts including 141.4 metres at 0.97% CuEq from 3.6 metres depth and 216.0 metres at 0.67% CuEq from 156 metres depth including a 64.1-metre high-grade core at 1.10% CuEq. Mineralization is now defined over 800 metres of strike length and 400-plus metres of vertical extent with the system open in both directions, and the newly confirmed eastern trend could meaningfully improve the open-pit strip ratio assumptions feeding into the Q4 2026 Pre-Feasibility Study — a completion milestone that would position North Island as a fully-priced M&A candidate in a copper market where the Jefferies-upgraded 2030 price target of $8/lb is now consensus.

headline: MITHRIL SILVER GOLD COPALQUIN: 225 g/t Ag, 4.01 g/t Au OVER 7.25m — ULTRA-HIGH-GRADE INTERVALS AS MRE UPDATE NEARS
source_name: Small Caps / Mithril Silver and Gold
snippet: Mithril Silver and Gold Limited (TSXV: MSG / ASX: MTH) released June 10 drilling results from the El Refugio target within the Copalquin District in Durango, Mexico — key intercept: RE26-013 returned 7.25 metres at 4.01 g/t Au and 225.1 g/t Ag (7.22 g/t AuEq) from 369.5 metres depth, including an ultra-high-grade section of 0.50 metres at 15.25 g/t Au and 533 g/t Ag, with six subparallel mineralised structures also confirmed outside the existing 2021 resource boundary at La Soledad. With 11,238 metres of the 25,000-metre 2026 drill program completed and an updated mineral resource estimate targeted for late June, Mithril's Copalquin District is approaching a near-term stock-re-rating catalyst at a time when silver royalty companies and mid-tier producers are aggressively building silver inventory ahead of a market projected to record its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit.

headline: GOLDSEEK JUNE 10 ASIAN METALS ROUNDUP: China's Physical Floor Bid Persists — Gold, Silver, Copper Data Update
snippet: GoldSeek's Asian Metals Market Update for June 10, 2026 covers pricing signals from the Chinese and broader Asian physical metals complex, noting that Asian physical buying has maintained a persistent floor bid in gold and copper despite Western paper-market pressure, with the differential between Asian physical premiums and COMEX/LME paper prices serving as an early indicator of where sentiment is heading. For self-directed investors tracking the current gold correction, the June 10 Asian data suggests the physical demand floor is firmer than the Western spot chart implies — consistent with PBOC data showing 60,000 oz added to Chinese reserves in May and China importing 790-plus tonnes of silver in early 2026 to support its solar and electronics industries.

headline: NOA LITHIUM BRINES RIO GRANDE: BOTH RIGS ACTIVE AT 168m, SALTA BRINE AQUIFER PFS TARGET YEAR-END 2026
source_name: Digital Media Net / NOA Lithium Brines
snippet: NOA Lithium Brines Inc. (TSXV: NOAL) reported June 11 that both drill rigs at the Rio Grande Project in Salta Province, Argentina are operating on schedule — Well RT-RG26-PW001 having reached 168 metres depth and Well RT-RG26-PW002 underway at 30 metres — targeting deep brine-bearing aquifers to support a Preliminary Feasibility Study by year-end 2026. NOA holds one of the largest lithium brine claim portfolios in the region not owned by a producing company, over 140,000 hectares across three prospective salars (Rio Grande, Arizaro, Salinas Grandes), positioning the company as a potential strategic acquisition target as battery material developers accelerate their Argentine lithium sourcing following the structural price recovery to above $24,000/t lithium carbonate.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: HOW WARSH MEASURES INFLATION COULD MATTER MORE THAN THE JUNE 17 RATE DECISION FOR GOLD
snippet: GoldSilver.com's pre-FOMC analysis argues that Kevin Warsh's documented preference for measuring inflation more broadly than headline CPI — incorporating asset prices and longer-duration expectations — could produce a meaningfully different real-yield calculation than markets currently model, with the measurement framework Warsh chooses potentially worth more to gold's price trajectory than whether he holds or signals a hike on June 17. The practical framework for investors entering the June 16–17 FOMC: the dot plot's rate path matters less than the specific inflation language Warsh uses in the press conference, because the choice of inflation anchor determines the real yield that is gold's primary driver — and a broader inflation measure would imply lower real yields than the current market-consensus CPI-based calculation.

headline: NEWMONT HITS 260-DAY MA SUPPORT — SCHAEFFER'S QUANTITATIVE MODEL FLAGS 55% ODDS OF 6% GAIN WITHIN ONE MONTH
snippet: A June 11 Schaeffer's Investment Research analysis highlighted that Newmont Corporation (NYSE: NEM), up 2.4% to $95.01, touched its 260-day moving average — triggering a quantitative setup that has appeared 11 times in the last decade, after which NEM was higher one month later 55% of the time averaging a 6% gain, implying a price target near $100.71. The analysis also noted that NEM's Schaeffer's Volatility Scorecard of 80 out of 100 suggests the stock has persistently realized higher volatility than options pricing implied — a condition where directional call options are structurally underpriced going into the Warsh FOMC week catalyst that could sharply re-rate the entire gold producer complex.

headline: COPPER AT CROSSROADS: IRAN CONFLICT THREATENS $12K PRICE FLOOR AS 600K-TONNE ANNUAL DEFICIT LOOMS THROUGH DECADE
snippet: Investing.com's June 2026 analysis explains why copper sits at a counterintuitive crossroads: structural demand forecasts from AI data centres, grid buildout, and electrification support a 600,000-tonne annual deficit through the decade, but the Iran conflict's inflationary effect on global industrial production costs threatens the $12,000/tonne price floor that defines economic viability for 40-plus copper projects currently in pre-construction permitting. The Hormuz resolution timeline is identified as the single most important near-term copper price variable — a deal closes before the inflation re-rating fully takes hold and COMEX copper bounces toward $6.65+/lb; if negotiations drag through July, the energy-inflation transmission mechanism compresses downstream construction and manufacturing demand for the metal most critical to the energy transition.

headline: U.S. GOLDMINING WHISTLER ALASKA: EQUIPMENT AHEAD OF SCHEDULE — $2.04B NPV PROJECT BEGINS DRILLING "WITHIN WEEKS"
snippet: U.S. GoldMining Inc. (NASDAQ: USGO) announced June 9 that all critical equipment and consumables have been mobilized to the Whistler Gold-Copper Project in Alaska ahead of schedule, with crews actively constructing drill pads at high-priority Whistler–Raintree targets and diamond core drilling expected to commence within weeks. The PEA for Whistler outlines an after-tax NPV5% of $2.04 billion, a 33% IRR, and a 2.1-year payback at base-case gold-copper prices — and with the project fully permitted in Alaska and the first holes of the 2026 campaign imminent, Whistler represents one of the highest-NPV undeveloped gold-copper projects in North America entering the drill bit at a moment when gold producers are aggressively seeking development-stage assets to replace depleting reserves.

headline: SIRIOS LAUNCHES 25,000m CHEECHOO PHASE 1 IN JAMES BAY — TWO RIGS TURNING, LIBS TECHNOLOGY DEPLOYED FOR RESOURCE UPDATE
snippet: Sirios Resources Inc. (TSXV: SOI) announced June 9 the launch of Phase 1 of its fully funded 25,000-metre drilling campaign at the Cheechoo Gold Project in the James Bay region of Quebec, with two drill rigs now mobilized on site and a third rig scheduled to join by end of June — the largest and most systematic campaign ever executed on the property, targeting three sectors to enable an updated resource estimate and support a planned PEA in H1 2027. In a technical first for the project, Sirios has deployed a LIBS (Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy) unit to analyze drill core directly on site, improving the precision of lithological logging and metallurgical understanding in real time — a capability that previous Cheechoo operators did not have, and which could identify high-grade domains that earlier resource models missed.
